findings.title: sol start --port does not propagate to the spawned server (advertised flag path is misleading)
findings.detail: The card's implementation note advertises `start`/`status` accepting `--port` "so lifecycle commands can target a non-default port", but on the `start` path the flag only drives the CLI's own printed port and health-probe URL (effective-port, lines 38-44, 115, 128, 130-135). The spawn command (lines 119-121: `nohup node <server> >> <log> 2>&1 & echo $!`) passes no env, and `exec-shell-capture` applies no env override, so the child only sees ambient SOL_PORT/PORT. Sol's server resolves its listen port exclusively from SOL_PORT/PORT env (packages/sol/src/cljs/open_hax/sol/infra/config.cljs:48 — no flag mechanism exists). Consequence: `eta-mu sol start --port 9000` without SOL_PORT set spawns sol actually listening on 8001, prints `sol started (pid X, port 9000)`, probes http://127.0.0.1:9000/health, fails, then prints `health: not yet reachable` and exits 0 while the healthy server sits on 8001. SOL_PORT env works (verified on the card's transcript), so DoD is met, but the delivered `--port`-on-start behavior is broken/misleading. Fix by injecting `SOL_PORT=<effective-port>` into the spawn env (and arguably SOL_HOST), or scope `--port` to `status` only — note the asymmetry is already visible in help text: `status` advertises `(--port, or SOL_PORT/PORT env)` (line 241) while `start` does not (line 232).

findings.title: Stale pidfile + pid reuse: sol stop can SIGTERM an unrelated process
findings.detail: `live-pid` (lines 78-85) trusts any live numeric pid from .eta-mu-sol/sol.pid via `kill -0`, and `stop-impl` (line 144) SIGTERMs it without verifying the process is actually sol (e.g. /proc/<pid>/cmdline containing the resolved server path). If sol crashes without `stop` and the pid is recycled, a later `eta-mu sol stop` kills an innocent process. Conventional pidfile caveat and low probability given start/stop manage the file, but the repo-root state dir is per-cwd and crash-without-stop is a realistic operator path; a cmdline check is a cheap guard.

findings.title: `sol start --port` never reaches the spawned server — CLI reports/probes the flag port while sol binds SOL_PORT/PORT env
findings.detail: start-impl (lines 117-121) builds the launch command as `nohup node <server> >> <log> 2>&1 & echo $!` and spawns it via child/exec-shell-capture, which passes no :env override (extern/child_process.cljs:68), so the child inherits only the ambient environment. Had 8000 been free, the command would have exited 0 with `health: not yet reachable at http://127.0.0.1:8991/health` while the server actually listened on 8000 — a false success signal. The card's implementation note promises `--port` on start 'so lifecycle commands can target a non-default port'; only the env-var path (used in the card's manual verification) actually does that. Fix by injecting the effective port into the spawn command (e.g. `SOL_PORT=<port> nohup node …`, ditto SOL_HOST if a host flag ever lands), or scope `--port` to status/probe only and say so in help text.

findings.title: sol stop can SIGTERM an unrelated process: pidfile liveness is checked with kill -0 only, no process-identity verification
findings.detail: live-pid (lines 87-94) trusts any pidfile whose pid passes `kill -0`, and stop-impl (lines 149-166) then SIGTERMs it. Reproduced live during this review: a stale `.eta-mu-sol/sol.pid` at the repo root named pid 685792, which was a live process but not sol (nothing listening on the probed port; the last real sol server in sol.log was a different pid). `sol start` refused to start ('sol is already running (pid 685792, port 8177)'), `sol status` reported 'process: running' with health unreachable, and `sol stop` sent SIGTERM to that foreign pid and reported success. After any pid recycle (reboot, long uptime), `stop` kills an arbitrary process and `start` is blocked by a phantom. The card's claim 'clears stale pidfiles' only holds when the stale pid is dead. Before SIGTERM, verify identity — e.g. /proc/<pid>/cmdline contains the resolved server path, or record the launched port in the state dir and require a matching /health — and have start treat a non-sol pid as stale.

findings.title: start/status report and probe the port resolved from current flags/env, not the port the running server actually bound
findings.detail: start-impl's already-running branch (line 124) prints `port <effective-port flags>` and status-impl (lines 168-179) health-probes health-url built from the *current* env/flags, while the state dir records only the pid. Observed live: with a server previously started under different env, `SOL_PORT=8177 sol start` printed 'sol is already running (pid 685792, port 8177)' and `sol status` probed 8177 and exited 1 ('health: unreachable') though the pid was alive. The port precedence contract is documented on the card, but the running server's actual bind port is recoverable at start time — recording it next to the pidfile (e.g. .eta-mu-sol/sol.port) would make 'already running' output and status probing honest instead of echoing whatever env happens to be set now.

findings.title: stop waits only 10s for exit while sol's own shutdown drain grace defaults to 25s
findings.detail: stop-impl's wait loop (lines 153-161) gives up after 20x0.5s=10s and exits 1 with 'did not exit within 10s; pidfile kept'. But packages/sol/src/cljs/open_hax/sol/infra/config.cljs sets :shutdown-grace-ms default 25000 (SIGTERM drain, per the server log '[shutdown] received SIGTERM; draining Sol'). Under in-flight load sol may legitimately take >10s to exit, producing a false failure from `sol stop` (recoverable by re-running, but noisy and confusing for operators). Align the wait with the server's drain grace or document the mismatch on the card.
